verdict: ACCEPT with findings: the guard does what the commit claims, in the right place; 2 mutants survive the shipped tests (test gaps, behaviour correct) and 3 edge cases of 'can never satisfy' are not covered (non-regular files, a file used as a parent directory, one inaccurate note sentence).

baseline.command: docker run --rm --network none --cpus 2 --memory 2g -u 1000:1000 --init (worktree mounted rw) python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_todo_templates.py tests/unit/test_todo_plan_cli.py tests/unit/test_todo_runtime.py
baseline.result: 143 passed (matches the author: 81 base for plan_cli+runtime + 62 in templates = 45 base + 17 new)
baseline.test_diff_removed_lines: only 2 import lines (load_template import and the Cli,... import tuple) - no assertion of any existing test was removed or edited; core/todo_plan.py and core/todo_runtime.py are untouched by the commit (diff 0 lines), so the item predicates are unchanged.

evidence: Live CLI probes (real `python -m core.todo_cli create --template code_change`, in a disposable container, own git repo): existing directory, './out', 'out/', 'out/.', 'deep/./sub', '.', symlink-to-directory -> exit 2 refused=impossible_path naming item=implement predicate=files_changed path=<normalised>; absolute and '..' (also 'deep/../out') -> exit 2 refused=invalid_plan (the plan's own _relative rule); duplicates 'app.py'+'app.py', 'app.py'+'./app.py', 'new.py'+'new.py/' -> exit 2 impossible_path path named.

No plan file: in every refused probe the --store directory did not exist AT ALL afterwards (not merely no *.json; no .lock sidecar either). Successful creates leave att.json + att.lock. Shipped tests assert only `not glob('*.json')`; I checked the stronger store-absent fact myself.

Own mutants for the directory case (not the author's `and False`): M6 lookup in cwd instead of workspace -> 5 shipped tests red; M7 `is_dir() and is_file()` (never fires) -> 3 red (directory-refused, free-plan-route, audit-is-one-function). Mutant M3 (no normalisation in duplicate key) -> 2 red; both restored.

Meaning-vs-shape probe: symlink to a directory IS refused as DIRECTORY (is_dir follows symlinks), and a directory that exists only after normalisation ('./out', 'out/.', 'deep/./sub') is refused under its normalised name. A path THROUGH a symlinked directory ('link_dir/f.txt') is accepted as existing, correctly, since it is a file.
refuses-an-impossible-path.caveat: Two directory-case mutants SURVIVE the shipped tests (see mutants M1, M2): the shipped directory test uses an EMPTY directory reached directly, so (a) a symlink-skipping guard and (b) a guard that only fires for empty directories both pass 62/62. Real behaviour is correct (probed: non-empty dir 'out' with a file and a symlink to it are refused); the tests just would not notice a regression.

evidence: Not-yet-existing 'docs/new.md', a mix of existing+new, a create-only plan ['a_new.py','b_new.py'] and a modify-only plan ['app.py'] all freeze (exit 0). Result carries paths={workspace, workspace_is_a_directory, declared, existing, not_yet_existing, notes}; create-only lists both under not_yet_existing with one note naming them and 'will have to CREATE'; modify-only has existing=['app.py'], notes=[]. A scope glob list containing an existing directory (['docs/**','out']) is not judged (scope is not a delta path) and freezes.

Transport confirmed in source: integrations/dsh-driver/runtime.mjs `todo_plan` execute -> `todo.call(args.attempt_id, ['create', ...])`; call() -> run() = JSON.parse(CLI stdout) then returns `{refused:true,...result}` for exit 2 else `result` unchanged, adding only `brief` if absent. No key projection, so the `paths` key reaches the todo_plan tool result. I read this; I did NOT run the .mjs tests or a live DSH todo_plan call, and runtime.todo.test.mjs has no assertion on `paths`.

Announcement is not an excuse, positive/negative pair driven through the CLI: freeze ['docs/new.md'] (announced) -> begin -> done WITHOUT creating it: outcome=fail, files_changed 'docs/new.md does not exist after the step'; then create docs/new.md -> done: outcome=pass. (Shipped test test_a_path_that_does_not_exist_yet_still_has_to_be_created... does the same; mutant M4 which BANS not-yet-existing paths reddens 8 tests, M5 which drops the `paths` key reddens 5.)
absent-is-announced-not-banned.caveat: A not-yet-existing path whose PARENT is an existing regular file ('app.py/x/y.txt') is classified not_yet_existing and its note says the step 'will have to CREATE' it - that can never be satisfied. Same blind spot for an existing non-regular file (FIFO) which is listed as 'existing' although _digest returns None for it, so files_changed would fail it forever. The commit only claims directories, so this is a boundary of the claim, not a regression.

evidence: Placement: check_declared_paths is the last statement of _plan_from_args; cmd_create calls it before `with store.lock(...)`/store.write. Mutant M8a (audit removed from _plan_from_args) -> 22 red; M8b (audit moved to after store.write, inside the lock) -> 6 red including every 'no plan file' assertion and the free-plan route. So the 'before the plan file exists' ordering is pinned by tests, not by inspection.

Not in from_stored/from_json: probe froze ['later'] (absent), then made 'later' a directory: `status` and `begin` still succeed (plan keeps running, not refused on rehydration); `done` fails honestly ('later does not exist after the step'). Only a RE-CREATE of the identical plan after the path became a directory is now refused with impossible_path (exit 2) instead of returning created:false - an idempotent-retry edge; the existing plan file stays intact (not stranded).
Legitimate plans freeze through the CLI: create-only, modify-only, mixed, symlink-to-file, dangling symlink, same path in two different items (shipped test) - all exit 0.

Workspace-absent: ghost workspace and workspace-is-a-file both exit 0 with workspace_is_a_directory=false, declared listed, existing=[]/not_yet_existing=[] and one note ('could not be looked up ... nothing was assumed'). Announced, not skipped.

Inaccuracy found: that note says 'no directory, duplicate-spelling or existence check was made', but the duplicate check is not workspace dependent and still fires: ghost workspace with ['out','out'] -> exit 2 impossible_path. Text only; behaviour is the stricter, correct one.
No other test changed meaning (see baseline): 143 passed, only import lines removed from the test file.

shapes.existing directory ('out'): item implement: files_changed.paths declares 'out', an existing DIRECTORY under workspace <ws>: the item requires every declared path to differ from its state at the start of the step, and a directory has no state to differ from - files_changed compares a file's digest, so this item could never pass and the attempt would run until someone abandoned it; declare the files inside it   [refused=impossible_path, item=implement, predicate=files_changed, path=out; exit 2]
shapes.absolute '/etc/passwd': item implement: files_changed.paths must be a relative path inside the workspace, got '/etc/passwd'   [refused=invalid_plan; exit 2]
shapes.'../x': item implement: files_changed.paths must be a relative path inside the workspace, got '../x'   [invalid_plan]
shapes.'deep/../out': item implement: files_changed.paths must be a relative path inside the workspace, got 'deep/../out'   [invalid_plan]
shapes.duplicate ['app.py','./app.py']: item implement: files_changed.paths declares 'app.py' twice ('app.py' and './app.py' are the same path once normalised): a list that repeats one file names fewer files than the director reads it as - the other file that was meant is not declared at all, and this item would judge a shorter list than intended   [impossible_path, path=app.py]
shapes.empty string ['']: item implement: files_changed.paths has the wrong type or is empty: ['']   [invalid_plan, pre-existing rule]

unverified: Did not run integrations/dsh-driver/runtime.todo.test.mjs (node) nor a live DSH `todo_plan` call: the claim that `paths` reaches the tool result rests on reading runtime.mjs (call()/run() return the CLI JSON unprojected) plus the CLI stdout, not on observing the tool output.

Tests assert `not glob('*.json')` for 'no plan file'; I verified the stronger 'store directory absent' only with my own live probes, not as a regression test. A mutant that audits inside the lock but before write (leaving an empty .lock) was not run and would likely pass the shipped tests.
Concurrency/race (path becomes a directory between audit and write; two creates racing) not examined: the audit runs outside the lock by design.

Case-insensitive filesystems, Windows separators, very long/unicode paths, permission-denied stat() (is_dir returns False on EACCES so such a directory would be announced as not_yet_existing) not probed.

Did not run the full repository suite; only the three todo test files (143 passed). The other 3 shipped templates (test_fix, docs_change) were exercised by the shipped tests, not by my probes (I used code_change and relied on the shipped investigate test).

Findings left unfixed by instruction (review only): non-regular existing files and a file-as-parent path are not refused; the workspace-absent note over-states what was skipped; M1/M2 need tests (a non-empty dir and a symlink-to-dir case).
